answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, limiting influence to reachable, independently supported nodes rather than self-issued identities. A sybil cluster connected to honest nodes by a sparse external cut has low conductance; escape and min-cut bounds constrain the walk mass it can capture, and thus its aggregate voting weight. A plume of colluding attestations cannot summon a zephyr of trust across a hollow boundary.
